**Direct answer:** Jürgen Aschoff studied medicine at the University of Bonn. Some sources suggest he also studied at other universities, so Bonn may not be the only one.

**Claims and support**

- Aschoff enrolled in medicine at the University of Bonn after finishing his Abitur. He said he did so "lacking a specific interest." I read this on the page itself.
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Aschoff

- He moved to the University of Göttingen in 1938 and worked on thermoregulation physiology under Hermann Rein. He received his venia legendi (teaching qualification) there in 1944 and became a professor in 1949. I read this on the Wikipedia page.
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Aschoff

- An obituary reportedly places him later at Göttingen, Würzburg and Heidelberg. I only saw this in a search-result summary and did not open the obituary.
  https://bioone.org/journals/the-auk/volume-117/issue-3/0004-8038_2000_117_0779_IMJRA_2.0.CO_2/IN-MEMORIAM-J%C3%9CRGEN-ASCHOFF-19131998/10.1642/0004-8038(2000)117%5B0779:IMJRA%5D2.0.CO;2.full

- Wikidata lists his education as Bonn, Heidelberg and Freiburg. This differs from the other sources, which don't mention Freiburg. I only saw this in a search-result summary and did not open the Wikidata page.
  https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q75270

**Caveats:** The Wikipedia page gives no dates for his Bonn studies and doesn't mention a medical degree. Wikidata's list suggests he may also have studied at Heidelberg or Freiburg. I did not resolve which university awarded his degree.
